answer_1.quote: We follow  and classify NLG tasks into three types: compression, creation, and transduction, and select typical tasks from each category to conduct experiments. For compression and creation, we choose summarization and dialogue response generation to measure the performance of UNIEVAL, as well as the ability to zero-shot to unseen dimensions. For transduction, we select data-to-text to test whether UNIEVAL has the ability to transfer to a new NLG task.
answer_1.outputs: generated summaries, dialogue responses, and data-to-text utterances

answer_2.quote: We compare UNIEVAL with several state-of-the-art evaluators. Notably, all the single-dimensional and unified evaluators are built on the same corpus.

answer_3.quote: We propose a unified multi-dimensional evaluator UNIEVAL for text generation tasks. UNIEVAL unifies all evaluation dimensions into a Boolean Question Answering (QA) Table... For instance, UNIEVAL can evaluate coherence in summarization by inputting a specific question, such as "Is this a coherent summary to the document?".

answer_4.quote: SummEval (Fabbri et al., 2021) is a meta-evaluation benchmark for summarization. For each summary to be evaluated, it provides human scores from four dimensions: fluency, coherence, consistency and relevance.
answer_4.guideline: The benchmark provides human scores from four dimensions: fluency, coherence, consistency and relevance.
